examples.solution_text:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$\angle ACB=166^{\circ}\div2=83^{\circ}$.
$\angle ADB=\angle ACB=83^{\circ}$ (angles at the circumference standing on the same arc).
Both vertices lie on the major arc, so both angles stand on the minor arc $AB$. Their different positions do not change their equal angles.

$\angle AOB=2\times31^{\circ}=62^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
$OA=OB$ (radii), so $\triangle OAB$ is isosceles and its base angles are equal.
$\angle OAB=(180^{\circ}-62^{\circ})\div2=59^{\circ}$.

$\angle ACB=90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle).
$\angle ABC=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-36.5^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$).
$\angle ABC=53.5^{\circ}$.

$\angle ACB=90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle), so $AB$ is the hypotenuse.
$BC=\sqrt{AB^2-AC^2}$ (Pythagoras).
$BC=\sqrt{18^2-7^2}=\sqrt{275}\approx16.58$ cm.

$C$ is on the major arc, so $\angle ACB$ stands on the minor arc.
Minor $\angle AOB=2\times67^{\circ}=134^{\circ}$.
Reflex $\angle AOB=360^{\circ}-134^{\circ}=226^{\circ}$.
$D$ is on the minor arc, so $\angle ADB$ stands on the major arc and matches the reflex centre angle.
$\angle ADB=226^{\circ}\div2=113^{\circ}$.
The two circumference angles have vertices on opposite arcs, so the same-arc equality property does not apply.

Let $\angle OCA=x$ and $\angle OCB=y$.
$OA=OC$ (radii), so $\triangle OAC$ is isosceles and $\angle OAC=x$.
$\angle AOD=x+x=2x$ (exterior angle of $\triangle OAC$).
$OB=OC$ (radii), so $\triangle OBC$ is isosceles and $\angle OBC=y$.
$\angle BOD=y+y=2y$ (exterior angle of $\triangle OBC$).
$D$ lies inside $\angle AOB$, so
$\angle AOB=\angle AOD+\angle BOD=2x+2y=2(x+y)$.
Since $\angle ACB=x+y$, $\angle AOB=2\angle ACB$.

existingExamples.reason: Correct source-supported halving and same-arc explanation. The diagram identifies the given centre angle and both vertices without revealing answers. Equations retain their left-hand sides, so no phantom gutter is needed. Plain solution prose and mathematics inherit blue.

Correct doubling followed by the taught equal-radii isosceles method. The diagram includes the given circumference angle and all required sides. Independent equations need no phantom gutter; solution ink is supplied by the renderer.

Correct semicircle and triangle-sum working with a geometrically consistent given angle. The question diagram does not disclose the derived right angle. Every equation has its own left-hand side; solution prose and mathematics inherit blue.

Correct source-supported semicircle-to-Pythagoras example with a correctly rounded result. Both given lengths are annotated, and the derived right angle is stated only in the solution. Independent equations require no phantom gutter; solution ink is automatic.

Correct minor/reflex conversion and major-arc halving. The diagram distinguishes vertices on opposite arcs and marks only the given angle. The explanation prevents misuse of same-arc equality. No relation-led continuation requires a gutter; solution ink is automatic.

Correct proof using equal radii, exterior angles and addition, matching the supplied scaffold. The diagram includes the centre-line extension and all proof arms; auxiliary angles are defined in editable solution text. All equations retain their left-hand sides and inherit blue.
